s5-status.title: Status & priority
s5-status.note: FAMILY SETS. These 20 concepts are two families used as chips and badges on work items: 14 statuses (status-*) and 6 priorities (priority, priority-*). Within ONE idea (classical, bold, pebbles or weird) draw the whole family in ONE shared vocabulary (a common container or gesture, the meaning carried by what changes inside it), so the set reads as a set. Between ideas the vocabularies differ. status-superseded (this one is the old one, replaced) and status-supersede (this one takes over) are two sides of the same relation: draw them as a pair. The priorities form a scale: critical > high > medium > low, and undefined is 'not ranked yet'; the scale must be readable without a label, at 20 px.

concepts.name: delivery
concepts.meaning: work handed over and arrived in users' hands

concepts.name: shipment
concepts.meaning: a parcel on its way: something packed and sent out

concepts.name: release
concepts.meaning: a numbered version going out to users (not the status chip, the act and the version)

concepts.name: beta
concepts.meaning: pre-release testing with a first circle of early users

concepts.name: test
concepts.meaning: trying something to see if it works: a check, an experiment

concepts.name: changelog
concepts.meaning: the written list of what changed between versions

concepts.name: backlog
concepts.meaning: the queue of work waiting to be picked up

concepts.name: flow
concepts.meaning: something moving smoothly through steps without blockage

concepts.name: history
concepts.meaning: past events in order: looking back through time

concepts.name: journal
concepts.meaning: a personal diary kept day after day

concepts.name: log
concepts.meaning: an append-only, chronological record of events

concepts.name: ledger
concepts.meaning: a book of accounts: entries kept in ruled columns

concepts.name: record
concepts.meaning: one entry kept on file: a fact written down (not a recording button)

concepts.name: inventory
concepts.meaning: an itemised stock of what exists, counted and listed

concepts.name: commitment
concepts.meaning: a promise to follow through: a pledge

concepts.name: decision
concepts.meaning: a choice made at a fork, taken and recorded

concepts.name: data
concepts.meaning: raw information held: records, values, numbers

concepts.name: database
concepts.meaning: where data is stored and structured: tables, rows

concepts.name: server
concepts.meaning: a machine in the back that answers requests

concepts.name: api
concepts.meaning: the contract through which two programs talk: endpoints, requests and answers

concepts.name: system
concepts.meaning: many parts working together as one whole

concepts.name: architecture
concepts.meaning: how the whole is structured: the plan of the building

concepts.name: integration
concepts.meaning: parts joined so they work with each other: a plug, a connection between services

concepts.name: agentic
concepts.meaning: an AI agent acting on its own, on your behalf, toward a goal

concepts.name: git
concepts.meaning: version control: the tool and its tree of changes

concepts.name: branch
concepts.meaning: a line of work diverging from the main line (git)

concepts.name: fork
concepts.meaning: a copy taken to go your own way (git fork); also a split in the road

concepts.name: merge
concepts.meaning: two lines of work coming together into one

concepts.name: node
concepts.meaning: a point in a graph: a vertex

concepts.name: graph
concepts.meaning: nodes connected by edges: a network

concepts.name: edge
concepts.meaning: the link between two nodes

concepts.name: node-add
concepts.meaning: add a node to the graph (the action)

concepts.name: node-new
concepts.meaning: a node that is newly created: fresh, just appeared (a state, distinct from node-add)

concepts.name: node-remove
concepts.meaning: remove a node from the graph (the action)

concepts.name: journey
concepts.meaning: a path travelled across steps and time, with a start and an arrival

concepts.name: overview
concepts.meaning: the whole picture at a glance: a bird's-eye summary

concepts.name: view
concepts.meaning: one way of looking at the content: a lens on the data

concepts.name: page
concepts.meaning: a single screen or document of the app or site

concepts.name: screens
concepts.meaning: the set of an app's screens seen together

concepts.name: layout
concepts.meaning: how things are arranged on a surface

concepts.name: pane
concepts.meaning: one panel of a split window

concepts.name: matrix
concepts.meaning: a grid of rows and columns crossing two dimensions

concepts.name: tooltip
concepts.meaning: a small floating hint that explains an element

concepts.name: enabled
concepts.meaning: switched on, available to use

concepts.name: disabled
concepts.meaning: present but unavailable: cannot be used

concepts.name: expand
concepts.meaning: open up to show more: unfold, bigger

concepts.name: collapse
concepts.meaning: fold up to hide detail: smaller

concepts.name: inform
concepts.meaning: tell, notify, make known: an information notice

concepts.name: affordance
concepts.meaning: a shape that shows what you can do with it: a handle, a button that looks pressable

concepts.name: quality
concepts.meaning: a high standard met: well made, checked, trustworthy

concepts.name: parity
concepts.meaning: the same thing on every platform: iOS, Android and web in step

concepts.name: code-quality
concepts.meaning: clean, readable, well-structured code

concepts.name: verification
concepts.meaning: checking that something is true or correct

concepts.name: quality-assurance
concepts.meaning: the process of checking quality before release: testing plus sign-off

concepts.name: acceptances
concepts.meaning: the conditions a piece of work must meet to be accepted, as a checklist

concepts.name: criterion
concepts.meaning: one standard a thing is judged against: a single check

concepts.name: finding
concepts.meaning: something discovered during an audit: a reported issue

concepts.name: resolved
concepts.meaning: an issue that has been dealt with and closed

concepts.name: solved
concepts.meaning: a problem solved: the answer found

concepts.name: fixed
concepts.meaning: something broken, now mended

concepts.name: performance
concepts.meaning: speed and responsiveness: how fast it runs

concepts.name: efficiency
concepts.meaning: the most result for the least waste

concepts.name: reliability
concepts.meaning: can be counted on: works every time, stays up

concepts.name: observability
concepts.meaning: seeing inside a running system through its signals (logs, metrics, traces)

concepts.name: monitoring
concepts.meaning: watching something continuously, ready for a signal to go off

concepts.name: status-idea
concepts.meaning: a spark, just an idea, not yet planned

concepts.name: status-backlog
concepts.meaning: accepted and waiting in the queue

concepts.name: status-development
concepts.meaning: being built right now

concepts.name: status-release
concepts.meaning: built and on its way out: being shipped, awaiting review

concepts.name: status-blocked
concepts.meaning: stuck, cannot move on until something is solved

concepts.name: status-live
concepts.meaning: in production, in users' hands, running

concepts.name: status-archived
concepts.meaning: put away, kept but no longer active

concepts.name: status-deprecated
concepts.meaning: still there but on its way out: do not use any more

concepts.name: status-warning
concepts.meaning: a caution state: attention needed

concepts.name: status-superseded
concepts.meaning: replaced by something newer: this is the old one

concepts.name: status-supersede
concepts.meaning: the act of replacing: this one takes the place of an older one

concepts.name: status-approved
concepts.meaning: accepted, validated, signed off

concepts.name: status-rejected
concepts.meaning: refused, turned down

concepts.name: status-draft
concepts.meaning: a work in progress, not final, unpublished

concepts.name: priority
concepts.meaning: what comes first: ranking by importance (the general concept)

concepts.name: priority-critical
concepts.meaning: top of the scale: drop everything

concepts.name: priority-high
concepts.meaning: important, soon

concepts.name: priority-medium
concepts.meaning: middle of the scale: normal

concepts.name: priority-low
concepts.meaning: bottom of the scale: when there is time

concepts.name: priority-undefined
concepts.meaning: not ranked yet: priority unknown

concepts.name: security
concepts.meaning: protection against attackers

concepts.name: privacy
concepts.meaning: what is kept to oneself, shielded from others' eyes

concepts.name: data-protection
concepts.meaning: the care taken of personal data and the rights of its owner

concepts.name: gdpr
concepts.meaning: the European data-protection regulation, a legal framework (do not copy the EU flag or its ring of stars)

concepts.name: safety
concepts.meaning: being kept from harm: a safe place, a net under you

concepts.name: store-compliance
concepts.meaning: meeting the rules of the app stores to be allowed in

concepts.name: risk
concepts.meaning: something that might go wrong: a chance of harm

concepts.name: health
concepts.meaning: the vitals of a person or a system: is it well

concepts.name: diagnosis
concepts.meaning: identifying what is wrong by examining signs

concepts.name: doctor
concepts.meaning: the practitioner who cares for health (no face, no cross: a stethoscope-level reading)

concepts.name: therapeutic
concepts.meaning: that which heals or soothes: a care practice

concepts.name: wellness
concepts.meaning: being well in body and mind: balance, calm, vitality

concepts.name: accessibility
concepts.meaning: usable by everyone, whatever their abilities

concepts.name: inclusion
concepts.meaning: everyone has a place: welcoming difference

concepts.name: anxiety
concepts.meaning: worry, tension: a mind racing, a tight chest

concepts.name: avoid-hassles
concepts.meaning: no trouble: friction removed, a smooth path

concepts.name: simplify
concepts.meaning: make less complex: fewer parts, stripped down

concepts.name: organize
concepts.meaning: put things in order: sort, group, tidy

concepts.name: reduce-effort
concepts.meaning: less work needed: lighter, easier, a shortcut

concepts.name: variety
concepts.meaning: many different kinds: a mix, a range

concepts.name: sensorial
concepts.meaning: felt through the senses: touch, sound, sight, smell, taste

concepts.name: aesthetics
concepts.meaning: beauty: form pleasing to the eye, taste

concepts.name: attractiveness
concepts.meaning: what draws you in: appeal, charm

concepts.name: fun
concepts.meaning: playful joy, lightness, a smile

concepts.name: entertainment
concepts.meaning: something that holds attention and amuses: a show, play

concepts.name: reward
concepts.meaning: a prize for effort

concepts.name: badge-value
concepts.meaning: the worth of an earned badge or achievement

concepts.name: recognition
concepts.meaning: being seen and acknowledged for what you did

concepts.name: belonging
concepts.meaning: being part of a group, having a place in it

concepts.name: community
concepts.meaning: a group of people together, sharing something

concepts.name: hope
concepts.meaning: expecting good to come: a light ahead

concepts.name: nostalgia
concepts.meaning: longing for the past: a memory warmed by time

concepts.name: heirloom
concepts.meaning: an object passed down through generations

concepts.name: legacy
concepts.meaning: what you leave behind for those who come after

concepts.name: debt
concepts.meaning: something owed: the weight of an obligation

concepts.name: transcendence
concepts.meaning: going beyond the ordinary: rising above

concepts.name: money
concepts.meaning: currency, cost, what things are worth

concepts.name: saving
concepts.meaning: putting aside for later: thrift, keeping

concepts.name: success
concepts.meaning: a goal reached: achievement

concepts.name: self-actualization
concepts.meaning: becoming the fullest version of yourself: growth toward your potential

concepts.name: motivation
concepts.meaning: the drive that makes you start and keep going
